# K2 Pro Creality Print/Cloud Klipper Estimator build

Status: hybrid wrapper tested locally against single-color and CFS files,
enabled in nine K2 Pro 0.4 process profiles in Creality Print and used to
migrate 17 existing printer-side G-code files. It is a Windows post-process
tool and is not installed as a printer daemon.

## Purpose

This package is based on the official `klipper_estimator` v3.7.3 source. The
test build adds recognition for headers in these forms:

```text
; generated by Creality_Print V7.2.0.5226 on ...
; generated by Creality_Cloud_Slicer V7.1.0.0 on ...
```

It then uses the existing Orca/Prusa-style metadata processor to update the
time comment and existing `M73` progress commands.

## K2 Pro hybrid calibration

Klipper Estimator is used as the motion-time base only when the file has no
real tool transition. If the original G-code changes from one `Tn` tool to
another, the PowerShell stage keeps Creality's original CFS-aware `M73`
timeline. This prevents retract, purge and tool-change time from disappearing.

Both paths add a calibrated 110-second median residual. It was derived from
nine completed single-color jobs in Moonraker history. Leave-one-out testing
reduced mean absolute error from about 158 seconds for raw Klipper Estimator
to about 94 seconds. The two completed CFS jobs were about 12 and 25 minutes
too short with raw Klipper Estimator; the hybrid estimates are within about
98 and 111 seconds of their recorded print durations.

The offset is stored in `K2Pro-Time-Calibration.json`. The correction applied
to `M73 R` decreases with remaining progress and is zero at `P100`. The total
comment receives the exact full offset.

## K2 Pro compatibility override

Creality's Klipper fork treats `[gcode_arcs] resolution: 0.012` as a chord
error and internally limits arc segments to roughly 0.1-1.0 mm. Upstream
Klipper Estimator treats the same value as a fixed 0.012 mm segment length.
Using the raw Moonraker dump therefore makes analysis unnecessarily slow.

The wrapper applies:

```text
mm_per_arc_segment=0.9
```

This was derived from the real vendor arc implementation and 11,356 arcs in a
completed K2 Pro G-code file. It does not change the printer configuration.

The wrapper normally refreshes motion limits from Moonraker. If the printer is
temporarily offline, it falls back to the included last-known-good K2 Pro
configuration instead of failing the Creality Print export.

## Test evidence

- Source unit test: passed.
- Real file: 3,018,688 bytes and 101,667 lines.
- Processing time through the final installed wrapper: under 2 seconds.
- Processing time with the corrected setting on the K2 ARMv7 host: about 2 seconds.
- Changed common lines: 71 total.
- Expected changes: 70 `M73` lines and one estimated-time comment.
- Unexpected changes: none.
- Slicer estimate: 40:14.
- Raw estimator result: about 40:39.
- Hybrid result: 42:29.
- Two completed-print records: about 41:34 and 42:40 print duration, plus
  variable preparation/AI time.

The result remains a static print estimate. Heating, homing, flow calibration,
AI preparation, pauses and user speed changes cannot be predicted exactly.
CFS operations are retained from Creality's timeline instead of being treated
as zero-time motion commands.

The Creality Cloud Slicer path was separately unit-tested and then validated
against `Mini Whistle_05200018.gcode`: 79 existing `M73` lines and one
estimated-time comment changed, with no motion or machine command changes.
All 17 existing G-code files passed the same strict comparison before their
atomic printer-side replacement. The originals remain in a timestamped backup.

## Current Windows setup

The stable installed command is:

```text
"C:\Users\bluec\AppData\Local\K2ProTools\klipper-estimator\K2Pro-CrealityPrint-Estimator.cmd"
```

It is enabled in the seven standard K2 Pro 0.4 process profiles from 0.08 mm
through 0.28 mm, including HueForge, and the two existing user copies at
0.12 mm and 0.16 mm. Structured JSON edits were used and all nine profiles
were parsed again after the change. Original profile copies are stored under
`C:\Users\bluec\AppData\Local\K2ProTools\backups`.

The slicer appends the generated G-code path as the first argument. The wrapper
keeps a temporary original, retrieves current motion limits from K2 Pro
Moonraker and falls back to its included last-known-good cache if the printer
is unavailable during export. After the estimator pass it runs
`K2Pro-Hybrid-Time.ps1`. Any failure restores the original file. A final
`K2PRO_HYBRID_TIME` marker makes repeated calls idempotent.

To undo it, remove `post_process` from those process profiles or restore the
timestamped profile backup. No printer-side uninstall is required.

## Provenance

- Upstream: https://github.com/Annex-Engineering/klipper_estimator
- Base version: v3.7.3
- Upstream license: MIT (`LICENSE.txt` is included)
- Local change: Creality Print and Creality Cloud Slicer header detection,
  matching unit tests, and routing both formats through the existing
  Prusa/Orca metadata processor.
